title: First customer workflow: published-source baseline

parent.remaining: All six parent acceptance requirements retain their current unaccepted state; this child audit does not substitute for the connected journey or human trial.

summary: The core workflow has substantive implementation and passing controlled tests. The first demonstrated recovery gap is manual opportunity creation: an audit failure can leave a saved opportunity and retry creates another. The full connected customer journey and an observed new-user trial remain unverified.

evidenceBoundary.demo: Fictional session-local runtime, not connected application records.
evidenceBoundary.domainFixtures: Production service functions backed by AuthorizedMemorySupabase. Tenant-bound queries are exercised but this does not prove native constraints, RLS, PostgREST or Auth.
evidenceBoundary.nativeIsolatedTenant: Not executed in this bounded audit. Existing reference runner includes native PostgreSQL checks with explicitly narrower scope.
evidenceBoundary.hostedJourney: Not observed. No production records were read or mutated for the journey.
evidenceBoundary.providerCalls: No real provider transport or paid inference. Stripe/OpenRouter are stubbed by the focused test.
evidenceBoundary.humanTrial: Not conducted. Local test duration is not user setup time.

matrix.implemented: The canonical identity resolver reuses contact/company identities, then createOpportunity inserts a new opportunity. The admin POST authenticates and calls this owner.
matrix.evidence: test:business-workflows passed real domain-function calls against AuthorizedMemorySupabase. The demo check reviews a seeded import batch; it does not prove a fresh database import.
matrix.finding: Controlled audit failure leaves one saved opportunity while returning an error; retry saves a second opportunity for the same contact/company.
matrix.status: happy path covered by memory fixture; recovery gap reproduced

sources.meaning: POST has no stable create request identity; service errors become HTTP 400.

matrix.implemented: A stage transition is validated and conditionally updates the current stage. Onboarding is a reviewed plugin action with active assignees, current won state and explicit approval; winning a deal alone does not create onboarding tasks.
matrix.evidence: test:business-workflows passed creation, won transition, task proposal/approval, replay, inactive-assignee and disabled-plugin checks using the in-memory database double.
matrix.status: domain behavior covered by controlled fixture
matrix.nativeOrHostedProof: No authenticated fresh-workspace onboarding was observed.

sources.meaning: Fresh approval, plugin check, deterministic effect key and per-task receipts.

matrix.implemented: Tasks use the shared task owner. Today loads the operator queue, whose bounded task queries filter by pending/snoozed status, date horizon and source. Completion goes through the shared action executor.
matrix.evidence: The demo test passed Today/detail/Activity parity across six fictional scenarios. The business-workflow fixture passed domain task completion. Source inspection confirms the production read/write owners, but does not prove their complete browser journey or every task appears on Today immediately.
matrix.status: demo parity and memory-domain evidence; connected parity unverified
matrix.nativeOrHostedProof: No same-customer connected Today/detail/Activity/browser proof in this audit.

sources.meaning: Canonical task creation and dedupe handling.
Tenant-bound Today data and source unavailable states.

matrix.implemented: The invoice reviewer checks canonical customer identity and current provider account/mode. Draft execution requires the persisted approved action. Sending is a separate proposal and approval tied to the created invoice.
matrix.evidence: test:stripe-workflow passed with fake Stripe/OpenRouter transport and memory application database. Exact totals, partial-result retry and separate send approval are exercised.
matrix.status: domain behavior covered by controlled provider and database fixtures
matrix.nativeOrHostedProof: No live or sandbox Stripe call and no customer delivery occurred in this audit.

sources.meaning: Review identity, account, mode and invoice lines.
Approved draft execution and deterministic provider keys.
Separate send proposal for an executed complete draft.
Guarded invoice reads and propose-send adapter.

matrix.implemented: Onboarding and invoice actions checkpoint effects and reuse deterministic keys. Invoice test-mode receipts explicitly distinguish provider acceptance from actual delivery. Manual opportunity creation has a different recovery boundary and no per-intent replay identity.
matrix.evidence: Controlled invoice test recorded one creation, one line write and one send effect despite retries; these are fixture effects. Separate opportunity reproduction recorded saved counts 1 then 2 after audit failure and retry.
matrix.status: action replay covered in fixtures; opportunity-create retry gap demonstrated
matrix.nativeOrHostedProof: Concurrent native-database/HTTP replay for manual create remains required by the follow-up.

sources.meaning: Manual create currently lacks the same replay boundary.

matrix.stage: First use by a new user
matrix.implemented: A deterministic demo trial runs six fictional scenario packs.
matrix.evidence: test:first-value-business-journey passed; reported total 48.923247 milliseconds is local fixture execution. It cannot measure human setup, confusion, authenticated browser operation or production latency.
matrix.status: fictional demo verified; observed new-user trial unverified
matrix.nativeOrHostedProof: An observed new-user trial and controlled connected workspace journey are still needed.

checks.scope: Six fictional scenario packs; demo surface parity and recovery; local fixture timing.
Production identity/pipeline/workflow/task functions with memory database fixture; no native tenant/HTTP proof.
Production invoice functions with memory database and deterministic transport; no real send.
Reproduces current defect; does not assert the workflow is fixed.

testExecution: All three npm test suites ran through agent:run and resources:run in the claimed worker using its own exact-lock npm ci install. The small failure reproduction ran directly with the same worker tsx.

referenceChecksReviewed.status: source inspected; full runner not executed in this audit
referenceChecksReviewed.meaning: Runs 13 separate checks, including native PostgreSQL work completion; collects and cross-checks selected artifacts. Its limits explicitly exclude hosted provider proof, Auth delivery, PostgREST and human timings. It is not one freshly authenticated customer journey end to end.

referenceChecksReviewed.status: source inspected; browser not run in this audit
referenceChecksReviewed.meaning: Routes **/api/admin/** to controlled responses. This proves UI behavior against stubs when run; it is not proof of connected persistence.

referenceChecksReviewed.status: source inspected; opt-in provider test not run
referenceChecksReviewed.meaning: Uses real Stripe test transport when explicitly configured, with an in-memory application database. Neither hosted database nor real customer delivery is implied.

releaseComparison.pipelineComparison: Read-only git diff from approved main for pipeline.ts and its POST route was empty. The reproduced manual-create boundary is unchanged in that observed release checkout.
releaseComparison.limits: Receipt candidate differs from the later checkout head; verification from the receipt is not attributed to the later head. The release owner retains release verification, migration and deployment work. No release or deployment acceptance is inferred here.

firstDemonstratedGap.severity: Recoverability defect on the first manual write; no observed hosted incident or claim that every create fails.

reproduction.environment: in-memory database double; production domain function
reproduction.firstError: Error: Audit write failed: Controlled audit failure
reproduction.limitation: No native database, HTTP route or hosted customer observation. Reproduction verifies service orchestration under the controlled adapter.

steps: Use a fictional tenant and production createOpportunity with the memory adapter.
Inject audit_log insert failure and submit one manual opportunity.
Observe thrown audit error and one already-saved opportunity.
Recover audit writes and repeat the same submission.
Observe two opportunities with one canonical contact/company pair.
firstDemonstratedGap.nextAction: Add stable per-intent create replay handling in the existing owner and adapters, with durable/reconcilable audit. Prove lost response, post-insert audit failure, concurrent retries, changed payload, tenant isolation and a deliberate second intent using native/API checks.
firstDemonstratedGap.scope: One bounded follow-up card, high priority / Next. No application fix is included in this research delivery.

verificationLimits: No browser journey was run. Source and domain-test success are not complete browser acceptance.
No complete native/hosted isolated-tenant customer-to-invoice journey was established.
No new-user observation, paid model call, provider send, purchase, migration or deployment occurred.
